title: Observation delays can bias inference of selective advantage in evolutionary competition
summary: Relative-frequency trajectories are often used to infer selective advantage in competing biological populations. A common empirical approach is to fit a linear function to the logit-transformed frequency of an invading type and interpret the slope as the relative advantage. Here we test how this estimator is affected when the competing types are observed after type-specific delays. We use SARS-CoV-2 variant replacement in the United Kingdom as empirical motivation and study the mechanism with simple two-type models.
